messages:
priya (eng-platform): Heads-up — saw a dedicated tenant get its burst credits revoked mid-spike and their requests went 429 despite reserved throughput being under limit. Console shows "Reserved: 100 rps, Active: 80 rps, Burst credits: 0". Is that expected? Anyone seen per-key instantaneous revocation behavior like this?

jake (sre): yea saw traces — requests were routed to fallback causing retries. I think we evicted their burst because node-level isolation triggered (no spare slots) and we prioritised fairness.

maria (eng-platform): clarification — our policy is supposed to allow soft-degrade: if reserved available, use it; otherwise consume burst until credits exhausted. We shouldn't 429 while reserved remains. Can you paste the headers from the client?

priya (eng-platform): headers: `X-Reserved-RPS: 100`, `X-Reserved-Used: 80`, `X-Burst-Credits: 0`, `X-Quota-Mode: burst-revoked` — client saw `HTTP/1.1 429 {"error":"dedicated_quota_exceeded"}`

sam (runtime): interesting — the serving node had an inflight_count lock due to a tenant ejection flow. When ejection runs, we mark tenant as "soft-block" which prevents new streams from queuing; looks like reserved slots were not considered during ejection.

maria (eng-platform): that's a bug if true. The intended behavior: ejection should only block burst allocation, not reserved throughput. File a quick issue?

lucas (observability): i can pull traces and dashboard for tenant-1789. We don't currently surface "burst vs reserved" allocation per-request in logs; we have aggregate counters. Suggest adding `allocation_type` tag (reserved|burst|fallback) to spans.

amy (product): from a UX perspective customers see 429 and think dedicated is broken. Console should show a timeline: reserved usage vs burst depletion + an explanation. Maybe also expose "grace queue" length.

kevin (billing): note: if we silently shift them to fallback (hosted) we might bill differently. Need to ensure billing tags carry whether request served by reserved or fallback.

jake (sre): proposed short-term mitigation: when ejection is in-flight, allow a small reserved-only admission path (rate-limit by reserved-rps) that bypasses burst checks. That prevents all 429s.

maria (eng-platform): sounds reasonable. Also need an event emitted to console and telemetry when burst revocation happens with reason (node_eject / admin_revoke / billing).

lucas (observability): I'll add allocation_type + revocation_reason to traces and logs. We also need a histogram of time-to-recover-burst for customers.

priya (eng-platform): i'll open an RFC for: 1) change ejection to preserve reserved admission; 2) console timeline & billing tag; 3) telemetry fields. Also adding a short line to API docs about headers returned on quota decisions.

ops-bot: Created issue #ENG-4721 (ejection-reserved-admission) assigned to @sam.

sam (runtime): ack — will prep a patch to skip burst-block for reserved requests. ETA EOD tomorrow.

maria (eng-platform): thanks. priya please add a small alert rule to console: high 429 spikes for dedicated tenants flagged while burst_credit=0.

priya (eng-platform): will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
